Config Compare

Compare how a published service is configured on two FortiWeb appliances — policy, virtual server, pool, certificates, content routing, allow lists and the web protection profile — from a simple source;policy;destination list, without writing anything.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view protection.view appliances.view
📍 WhereOperations → Troubleshooting → Config Compare (the Global block in the Global ADOM; live in the FortiWeb ADOM) (URL /compare)

What is it?#

Config Compare checks whether a service is configured the same on two FortiWeb appliances, and if not, exactly what differs. You give it one line per service — source;policy;destination — and SATOM reads every object behind the server policy on both boxes and subtracts them. It is the natural check after cloning a policy or before a migration, and it writes nothing.

What does it do?#

  • Reads the full dependency tree of the named server policy on the source and on the destination: virtual server, server pool and members, certificates, content routing, allow lists, the web protection profile and their sub-tables.
  • Pairs objects by the field that references them, not by name. An object that landed under a different name on the destination is reported as renamed, not as one object missing plus another one added.
  • Compares a web protection profile as one package: object counts and a fingerprint per side, −removed ~changed +added, and which sub-profiles differ — never one row per signature or entry.
  • Compares symmetrically: a setting only the destination has is reported just like one only the source has. Per-device bookkeeping (row ids) is ignored, and enable/True, 80/"80" and absent/empty count as the same value.
  • Gives each line one verdict: identical, differs, missing or error, plus a summary for the whole run.
  • Produces a tab-separated export with one line per difference.

Requirements#

  • Both appliances are FortiWebs registered in SATOM and visible in the current ADOM. Each side is identified by its SATOM name or its host (not case-sensitive).
  • SATOM must be able to reach both appliances' REST API — the comparison reads live, it does not use the local copy.
  • No device needs to be selected and no workspace tab needs to be open.

Permissions#

Opening and running the page needs the legacy view permission, which any granular view key grants — for example network.view, protection.view, appliances.view, monitoring.view or operations.view. All system profiles, including Viewer, have it. A user with none of them gets the 403 page, and the sidebar entry is shown only to users who can open the page.

Only appliances visible to you (current ADOM, maintenance rules) can be named in the list.

How to use#

  1. Open Operations → Troubleshooting → Config Compare (Global ADOM or FortiWeb ADOM; until 2026-10-14 it sat under Operations → Troubleshooting in the FortiWeb ADOM).
  2. In One service per line, enter lines such as fweb-01;spol-shop;fweb-02, or use …or upload the file (a file replaces the text box, and the box is refilled with the file so you can see what ran).
  3. Optionally change Time budget (s) (10 to 600, default 180).
  4. Click Compare. Reset clears the form.
  5. Read the Summary card: verdict counts, elapsed time, lines skipped or not treated as data, and Appliances read: (a red badge means SATOM could not connect; hover for the reason).
  6. Read each line's card: verdict, source ↔ destination, policy name, state counts, and a table with Object, Role (field), State, On and On . Differing fields are listed under each object.
  7. Copy the Export (tab-separated — one line per difference) box into a spreadsheet if needed.

Reading the states#

State Meaning
same Paired object, same name, no differing field
renamed Paired by role, different name, no other difference
changed Paired object with at least one differing field
only on source Present only on the source
only on destination Present only on the destination

A line is identical only if every row is same. missing means one box does not have the server policy at all. error means the line could not be compared (see Troubleshooting).

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
One service per line source;policy;destination. Lines starting with # are ignored; a format header such as source;policy;destination is skipped and listed. Up to 100 lines per run. Yes (or a file) fweb-01;spol-shop;fweb-02
…or upload the file Plain-text list, at most 256 KB. Non-UTF-8 files are read as latin-1 with a warning. No services.txt
Time budget (s) Stop starting new lines after this many seconds; lines not reached are listed by name. Clamped to 10–600. No (180) 300

Example#

🧪Example — Validate a migrated shop service

Input:

# source;policy;destination
fweb-01;spol-shop;fweb-02
fweb-01;spol-api;fweb-02

Result: spol-shop is differs — the web protection profile row is renamed (wpp-shop on fweb-01, wpp-shop-02 on fweb-02) with contents identical, and the server pool row is changed: the one differing field is listed under it with both values. spol-api is missing: the policy is not configured on fweb-02 at all — there is nothing to compare against.

Result#

  • Nothing is written to any appliance or to SATOM's configuration store.
  • Each run is recorded in the audit log as config.compare with the number of lines, verdict totals, elapsed time and whether the budget was hit — the run reads full policy trees, so it is audited even though it is read-only.

Troubleshooting#

"nothing to compare — one line per service, 'source;policy;destination'"#

The text box and file were empty, or contained only comments. Enter at least one line.

"this line has no destination — a comparison needs both sides"#

Add the destination appliance as the third field.

"expected 'source;policy;destination' — this line has N fields separated by ';'"#

Fix the line format. Related: no source appliance on this line, no server policy on this line.

"no appliance is registered as '' in this ADOM"#

Possible causes - Typo, the device is in another ADOM, or it is in maintenance mode.

Solution 1. Use the SATOM name or host shown in Appliances, or switch to the Global ADOM.

" is a — this check reads FortiWeb server policies"#

Only FortiWeb appliances can be compared.

" is registered on the placeholder host — it is a retired device, not something to probe"#

The appliance is a retired entry; use the current device.

"neither nor has a server policy called ''"#

Check the policy name (it is the server policy's name on the device).

": could not connect: …" or "could not read the policy tree: …"#

Possible causes - The appliance is unreachable, its credentials are wrong, or its API refused the read.

Solution 1. Check connectivity in Appliances and run the line again.

"The time budget expired. The lines below were NOT compared:"#

Raise Time budget (s) or split the file; each line is two full dependency-tree reads.

" is larger than 256 KB — this page takes a list of services, not a config dump"#

Upload only the service list.

"N more differing field(s) not shown — …"#

An object has more than 40 differing fields; only the first 40 are shown on the page. The export contains all of them.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the export now lists every differing field; before, it was cut to the same 40 fields as the page.

Advanced#

Advanced How the comparison is built

The dependency walk is the same one the policy-clone planner uses, so Config Compare and the clone report agree on what a service consists of. Sources are read before destinations on every line. Children are paired per reference field: if a field names exactly one object on each side they are counterparts whatever their names; if it names several, they are paired by name. Sub-table rows are matched on their key fields, or on their whole content when the table has none — never on the appliance-assigned id. A renamed object's own name field and the parent's reference to it are not reported again as changes.

Advanced Export columns

lineno, source, policy, destination, verdict, object, role, state, src_name, dst_name, field, src_value, dst_value. A web protection profile adds a package line (object count and fingerprint per side) and one package:<sub-profile> line per differing sub-profile.

#config compare#compare source destination#drift#migration check#policy diff#wpp package#renamed#tsv export
